stem.text: The function g is differentiable for all real numbers, and selected values of g and its derivative are given in the table. Find \( \lim_{x \to 7} \left(3 g(x) - 7\right) \), and justify your answer.

answer_key.label: The limit is -25, because g is differentiable at \( x = 7 \), so it is continuous there, and \( \lim_{x \to 7} g(x) = g(7) = -6 \).

worked_solution.text: g is differentiable at \( x = 7 \), so it is continuous there.
By the limit laws the limit is 3(-6) - 7 = -25.
worked_solution.rule_named: sum and constant multiple limit laws
